Preserve the accepted runner, robustness compiler, scoring compiler, no-fit wrapper, cumulative supervisor, MapLight runner, model runtime, candidates, features, parameters, seeds, groups, fits, predictions, metrics, gates, clips, selection token, and no-runner-up rule byte-for-byte.

supervisor_exception_protocol.validation: Require exactly the 13 accepted ResourceObservation fields with no extras: finite nonnegative wall, CPU, and GPU values; nonnegative integer storage, RSS, checkpoint, descendant, detached, and warning values; an integer-or-null return code; and exact booleans. The four hard-resource reason strings are classified only after this validation. A missing or malformed observation after claim consumption is FAILED and never resource-aborted; before claim consumption the pre-consumption rule applies and no terminal is fabricated.
supervisor_exception_protocol.scientific_or_underpowered_success: Require return_code to be the integer zero and not a boolean; checkpoints_acknowledged and descendant_processes_observed both greater than zero; cleanup_complete, network_namespace_isolated, and gpu_environment_hidden all true; gpu_hours, detached_children_observed, and warnings_observed all zero; and every observed wall, CPU, storage, and simultaneous-RSS value within the frozen parent hard limits before the cumulative seal rule is applied.

terminal_taxonomy.underpowered_rule: Only the compiler's exact RobustnessExecutionUnderpowered exception may produce UNDERPOWERED. It must occur after claim consumption and allowed official source parsing but before any model fit, prediction, baseline open, selection token, or development metric.
terminal_taxonomy.cleanup_rule: Any cleanup defect changes a scientific or underpowered status to FAILED. Unknown supervisor reasons fail closed as FAILED and can never become a scientific or resource success.

aggregate_accounting.semantic_rule: Counters record authoritative capability crossings, not operating-system read syscalls or repeated in-memory parsing. Each physical official source file opened into a trusted compiler counts its rows or values once for that compiler; a later independent compiler or scorer open counts again. The legacy official_source_rows_opened counter means direct endpoint rows only, official_target_values_opened means finite central point values only, and the legacy official_feature_identity_rows_opened, official_feature_matrix_rows_opened, and official_feature_rows_opened counters cover only the raw source-to-compiler crossing. Raw group-fold rows, finite reported-bound values, generated model features, generated model folds, generated predictions reopened for scoring, scoring truth, training targets, and baseline predictions use separate granular counters. Copying or reparsing bytes already held inside one trusted component does not create another open.

aggregate_accounting.failure_rule: A failed or resource-aborted terminal preserves every aggregate counter recoverable from a validated staged manifest and marks accounting_complete false when an interrupted child makes an exact count unavailable. It may never invent zero work after work began.

supervision_and_publication.supervised_boundary: The accepted supervisor begins before claim consumption, owns the fixed publication staging root, measures every private compiler/model/scorer/diagnostic/cleanup operation, and receives the complete aggregate-only terminal payload after private cleanup. Any child or supervisor failure removes that fixed staging root before control returns.
supervision_and_publication.post_supervision_seal: A ResourceObservation cannot truthfully include its own later serialization. After either a successful ResourceObservation, a canonical exception observation once valid claim consumption is proven, or a missing or malformed exception observation after valid claim consumption for an accounting-incomplete FAILED terminal only, the outer process may only clean exact owned aggregate staging, validate and add any available observation and the exact limits to an aggregate-only manifest, create the aggregate-only attempt_receipt.json that binds every other staged file, fsync the files and staging directory, make the fixed staging tree read-only, and atomically rename it without replacement to the final terminal. Scientific, underpowered, rejected, resource-aborted, and failed terminals all use this same bounded seal. This seal may open no official, baseline, model, truth, prediction, confirmatory, blinded-test, TDI, submission, leaderboard, portal, or upload capability.

cumulative_resource_rule.success_reservation: Before sealing a scientific, rejected, or underpowered payload, require observed wall_seconds plus the full 5-second seal reservation and observed cpu_seconds plus the full 5-second seal reservation to remain within the parent hard maxima. Require GPU hours exactly zero. The full 16,777,216-byte terminal reservation plus observed peak storage must remain within 51,200,000,000 bytes, and the outer seal process must remain within the 16,492,674,416-byte simultaneous-RSS maximum through atomic promotion. This worst-case reservation binds the otherwise self-referential receipt serialization without widening D-125.
cumulative_resource_rule.failure_rule: A canonical hard-limit observation publishes only RESOURCE_ABORTED; an ordinary canonical exception publishes only FAILED. A missing or malformed post-claim observation may publish only an accounting-incomplete FAILED terminal and never claim resource compliance. Every resource or failed terminal seal still obeys the 5-second wall, 5-second CPU, 16,777,216-byte terminal, 1,048,576-byte receipt, zero-GPU, and zero-additional-science limits.
cumulative_resource_rule.seal_failure_rule: A non-resource seal defect before final promotion permits exactly one same-invocation minimal FAILED seal after symlink-safe staging cleanup; this is evidence publication, not a scientific retry. A hard seal-resource breach permits exactly one minimal RESOURCE_ABORTED seal. If the final path already exists or the minimal seal or atomic promotion fails, clean fixed staging, retain the consumed claim, publish no replacement terminal, propagate a terminally blocking error, and never reinvoke the fixed claim or driver.

supervision_and_publication.aggregate_receipt: terminal/attempt_receipt.json is the aggregate attempt receipt and binds every other status-specific terminal file, the consumed claim, implementation lineage, accounting, cumulative supervision, cleanup, and denied authority. It is contained inside the one atomically promoted terminal root; no sibling receipt root is required or permitted.
supervision_and_publication.cleanup: Cleanup operates only on exact fixed children. A symlink at or below an owned cleanup root is unlinked and never followed. Interrupted fixed staging is removed by the supervisor on child failure and by the outer fail-closed publisher before any failure terminal.
supervision_and_publication.pre_consumption_failure: If supervision or the child fails before attempt_claim.json is atomically published, unlink without following any fixed claim-staging symlink, remove only the fixed claim staging path, fixed restricted root, fixed publication staging root, and empty fixed attempt root, require all five paths plus claim, receipt, and terminal absent, and propagate a fail-closed pre-consumption error. Do not fabricate a consumed claim or official terminal. The same fixed claim and driver are never reinvoked; progression stops unless the user separately authorizes a genuinely new scientific plan with a new contract, claim, and root, not a retry or replacement.
supervision_and_publication.final_attempt_file_set_precondition: The exact final attempt file set applies only after a valid attempt_claim.json proves that the sole claim was consumed.
